sense: knowledge or skill gained by doing

evidence: Plin. Ep. 1.20.12: quod mē docuit ūsus, magister ēgregius
Cic. de Or. 2.204: docuit nōs longa vīta ūsusque rērum maximārum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Often ūsus rērum, experience of affairs (M-O s.v. experience). “Experienced in” is perītus with the genitive (Traupman 152); “inexperienced”, imperītus (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Sall. Jug. 46.8: locōrum et mīlitiae (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Sallust and Tacitus; not in Cicero or Caesar (Lewis & Short).
Classically a trial or an attempt; in the sense “experience” from Vergil (G. 1.4) and in post-Augustan prose (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Adjiciam quod mē docuit ūsus, magister ēgregius.
phrases.english: I will add what experience, an excellent teacher, has taught me.

sources: Lewis & Short: usus · Lewis & Short: peritia · Lewis & Short: experientia
